A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same CoLA study and contain 17 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original CoLA evaluations on REC, RES, AVE and AVS in Section 4, with additional ablation and computational results in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark evaluations, ablations and computational measurements, including the CoLA results in Tables 1–7 and 11.

M1.justification: CoLA's dual pathways, hypernetwork, progressive feature propagation and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The Kronecker decomposition and asymmetric rank variants in Section 5.4 also remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate REC and RES on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg, and audio-visual tasks on AVE and AVSBench-S4. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical comparator membership, including both LoRA configurations, the visual-grounding methods, and LAViSH, STG-CMA and DG-SCT in their respective audio-visual comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–B retain identical backbones, evaluation metrics, dataset splits, training schedules, batch sizes and testing procedures.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D retain the same pathway-sharing, propagation, learned-scaling, rank-allocation, adaptation-direction and computational-overhead analyses, with no added or removed evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: All benchmark, ablation and computational results remain identical. For example, Tables 1–2 retain CoLA's averages of 83.4 for REC and 73.7 for RES, plus 80.7 for AVE and 80.9 for AVS.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same rank bound, Theorem 3.1 on the span of input-dependent updates, and gradient derivations. The Kronecker formulation is also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about cross-modal adaptation, performance and parameter efficiency, including the claimed first multi-task visual-grounding PEFT framework.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the experimental findings are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix D retain the same limitations concerning the nonmergeable inter-modal pathway and its runtime overhead.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, pseudocode, Appendix A hyperparameters and the code-access link are unchanged. The added studentship acknowledgement supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference entries are identical after matching across changed page breaks. Section 2 and the paper's positioning relative to prior research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 changes the corresponding author from Wish Suharitdamrong to Sara Atito and adds a doctoral-studentship acknowledgement before the Impact Statement. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new acknowledgement shifts the Impact Statement and reflows references across pages 10–12. Figures 1–6, Tables 1–12 and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a funding acknowledgement and updates correspondence, with limited reference reflow. These administrative refinements leave the scientific exposition, evidence, theory, reproducibility information and limitations unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
